what: EQT is the largest natural gas producer in the United States. It drills in the Marcellus and Utica shales in Appalachia and, unusually for a producer, also owns the gathering and transmission pipelines that move its gas.
customers: Utilities, industrial users, liquefied natural gas exporters and power generators, mostly in the eastern United States.
money: Natural gas, NGLs and oil sales
pipeline fees, including from third parties
moat: The lowest-cost large gas position in the country, with its own pipelines attached, so it does not depend on others for takeaway capacity.
risks: Natural gas prices are volatile and set earnings
Debt of about $6 billion against almost no cash
Appalachian pipeline capacity limits how much gas can reach premium markets
Revenue fell about 11% a year over three years before last year's rebound
opportunities: Revenue grew about 64% last year on higher gas prices
Data centre power demand and LNG exports are both raising US gas demand
Operating margin of 38% with the lowest cost structure among large gas producers
watch: Realised gas price against benchmark, and production volumes.
